Q: How can I make the .git folder not disappear in the build folder after npm run build? A:

This is what works for me. I added the ability to copy .gitignore as well and silenced the copyers so they don't make a mess in my terminal. Using CMD for this tho, so I had to change out "copy" for "xcopy"

"prebuild": "if not exist save_git mkdir save_git && xcopy .\\build\\.git .\\save_git\\.git /s /e /i >nul && copy .\\build\\.gitignore .\\save_git\\.gitignore >nul",
"postbuild": "xcopy .\\save_git\\.git .\\build\\.git /s /e /i >nul && copy .\\save_git\\.gitignore .\\build\\.gitignore >nul && rmdir /s /q save_git"

Q: Pydantic using a list from .env file with BaseSettings A:

Step 1: Update your .env file to

MY_LIST='["a","b"]'

Step 2: Incorporate SettingsConfigDict into your script

from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
import logging
import sys

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    my_list: list[str]
    # Removed Config and replaced with SettingsConfigDict
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
                env_file='.env', 
                env_file_encoding='utf-8')

try:
    settings = Settings()
    print(settings)

except Exception as e:
    logging.critical(f"required settings not provided, shutting down - {e}")
    sys.exit(1)

Step 3: Refresh the environment variables by running this from a shell session from your root directory (or directory with .env):

source .env

*Note: If you are continually updating your .env file, your environment variables are not automatically updated every time you run the python script in your current shell session.

Step 4: Run your script.

Versions:

  • Python 3.12.12

  • pydantic-settings 2.14

Q: How can I see how much storage an Aurora RDS instance is using? A:

Aurora does not have a notion of "disk storage". It uses a distributed volume to store your data, and what you are looking for is the Volume of that volume for your cluster. This is emitted as a Cloudwatch metrics, with the name VolumeBytesUsed.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Monitoring.html

That is the same metric used in your Billing computation as well. While you are there, do check the VolumeIOPS metrics as well (read and write) as they add to your billing as well.
